reasons: Rule is a 'missing' insurance clause and the record supports it: no insurance covenant appears in the General Matters provisions, while Sections 4(a)-(b) show on-premises installation and conversion/processing of Sparkling's data — exactly the vendor profile the playbook requires to be insured.

Inserted Section 20(k) tracks the model language and reaches the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, statutory workers' comp, certificates on request, surviving one year post-term), with the obligation correctly running against the counterparty (Garman).
Edit is minimal and well-placed: a single new subsection appended to the miscellaneous section with no alteration of the existing entire-agreement text.
Comment is accurate, in-tone, prefixed, explains the gap and cites both the preferred position and the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and an insurance obligation is present in the redline.
